title: “Monks, these ten perceptions, when developed and cultivated, are of great fruit, great benefit, merging with the deathless, having the deathless as their end. What…
content: “Monks, these ten perceptions, when developed and cultivated, are of great fruit, great benefit, merging with the deathless, having the deathless as their end. What ten? The perception of foulness, the perception of death, the perception of disgust with food, the perception of non-delight in the entire world, the perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering in impermanence, the perception of not-self in suffering, the perception of abandoning, the perception of dispassion, the perception of cessation. These ten perceptions, monks, when developed and cultivated, are of great fruit, great benefit, merging with the deathless, having the deathless as their end.”

title: “‘The destruction of the cord of continued existence, the destruction of the cord of continued existence,’ venerable sir, is said. What, venerable sir, is the…
content: “‘The destruction of the cord of continued existence, the destruction of the cord of continued existence,’ venerable sir, is said. What, venerable sir, is the cord of continued existence? What is the destruction of the cord of continued existence?” - “Rādha, whatever desire, lust, delight, craving, any engagement and clinging, any mental standpoints, attachments, underlying tendencies there are regarding form — that is called the cord of continued existence. Their destruction is the destruction of the cord of continued existence. Regarding feeling … perception … formations … Regarding consciousness, whatever desire, lust, delight, craving, any engagement and clinging, any mental standpoints, attachments, underlying tendencies there are — that is called the cord of continued existence. Their destruction is the destruction of the cord of continued existence.”

title: Elder Nāgasamāla: Adorned, dressed in fine clothes, They set the bait for Death. Then I attended to it, Reflecting wisely — The danger became clear,…
content:
Elder Nāgasamāla:

Adorned, dressed in fine clothes,
They set the bait for Death.

Then I attended to it,
Reflecting wisely —
The danger became clear,
I dwelt in disenchantment.

And my mind was liberated.
Seeing the Dhamma as it is,
I attained the three true knowledges,
Accomplishing the Buddha’s teaching.

title: “Aggivessana, what is untrained body and untrained mind? Here, Aggivessana, an untaught ordinary person experiences a pleasant feeling. Having felt that pleasant feeling, he lusts…
content: “Aggivessana, what is untrained body and untrained mind? Here, Aggivessana, an untaught ordinary person experiences a pleasant feeling. Having felt that pleasant feeling, he lusts after it and falls into lust for pleasure. If that pleasant feeling ceases, and due to its cessation, a painful feeling arises, he sorrows, grieves, laments, beats his breast, and becomes distraught. Aggivessana, that pleasant feeling arises for him and invades his mind and remains because the body is untrained. That painful feeling arises and invades his mind and remains because the mind is untrained. In this manner, for a person in whom either way — pleasant feeling arises and invades his mind because the body is untrained, and painful feeling arises and invades his mind because the mind is untrained — he is one with untrained body and untrained mind.”

title: Elder Mahā-Moggallāna: All conditioned things are impermanent — Having arisen, they must cease. After arising, they cease — Their calming is bliss. Those who see…
content:
Elder Mahā-Moggallāna:

All conditioned things are impermanent —
Having arisen, they must cease.
After arising, they cease —
Their calming is bliss.

Those who see the five aggregates
As other, not-self,
Penetrate the subtle,
Like a dart piercing a hair-tip.

Those who see the formations
As other, not-self,
Penetrate the subtle,
Like a dart piercing a hair-tip.

As if struck by a sword,
As if his head were on fire,
Mindful, a monk should go forth,
Abandoning sensual lust.

As if struck by a sword,
As if his head were on fire,
Mindful, a monk should go forth,
Abandoning craving for existence.

Not with such weakness,
Not with such little strength,
Can one attain Nibbāna,
Liberation from all bonds.

This young monk,
This supreme man,
Conquering Māra and his army,
Bears this last body.

title: “One in whom there are no underlying tendencies, Roots of unwholesome states well pulled out — That monk abandons the near and far shore, Like…
content:
“One in whom there are no underlying tendencies,
Roots of unwholesome states well pulled out —
That monk abandons the near and far shore,
Like a serpent sheds its worn-out skin.”

“One in whom there is nothing born of anguish,
That might lead back to this shore —
That monk abandons the near and far shore,
Like a serpent sheds its worn-out skin.”

“One in whom there is nothing born of craving,
That might lead to continued existence —
That monk abandons the near and far shore,
Like a serpent sheds its worn-out skin.”

“One who has abandoned the five hindrances,
Free from anguish, free from uncertainty,
Gone beyond the dart —
That monk abandons the near and far shore,
Like a serpent sheds its worn-out skin.”

title: “Monks, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. If a monk delights in those forms,…
content: “Monks, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, agreeable, pleasant, charming, connected with sensuality, enticing. If a monk delights in those forms, praises them, and dwells with lust for them — then, monks, this is called a monk who has gone into Māra’s domain, who has come under Māra’s control. Māra’s net has surrounded him. Bound by Māra, he is subject to the Evil One’s will … Monks, there are phenomena cognizable by the mind that are desirable … enticing. If a monk delights in those phenomena, praises them, and dwells with lust for them — then, monks, this is called a monk who has gone into Māra’s domain, who has come under Māra’s control. Māra’s net has surrounded him. Bound by Māra, he is subject to the Evil One’s will.”

title: “Monks, if anyone speaks of ‘a heap of the unwholesome,’ he would speak rightly of the five hindrances. The entire heap of the unwholesome, monks,…
content: “Monks, if anyone speaks of ‘a heap of the unwholesome,’ he would speak rightly of the five hindrances. The entire heap of the unwholesome, monks, is just the five hindrances. What five? The hindrance of sensual desire, the hindrance of ill-will, the hindrance of sloth and torpor, the hindrance of restlessness and remorse, the hindrance of doubt. If anyone speaks of ‘a heap of the unwholesome,’ he would speak rightly of the five hindrances. The entire heap of the unwholesome is just the five hindrances. If anyone speaks of ‘a heap of the wholesome,’ monks, he would speak rightly of the four foundations of mindfulness. The entire heap of the wholesome, monks, is just the four foundations of mindfulness. What four? Here, monks, a monk dwells contemplating the body as a body, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and sorrow in the world; dwells contemplating feelings as feelings … mind as mind … phenomena as phenomena, ardent, clearly comprehending, mindful, having removed covetousness and sorrow in the world. If anyone speaks of ‘a heap of the wholesome,’ he would speak rightly of the four foundations of mindfulness. The entire heap of the wholesome is just the four foundations of mindfulness.”

title: Elder Rājadatta: A monk came to a charnel ground, Saw a woman’s body Abandoned there, Discarded in the cemetery, Food for worms. Some become disenchanted…
content:
Elder Rājadatta:

A monk came to a charnel ground,
Saw a woman’s body
Abandoned there,
Discarded in the cemetery,
Food for worms.

Some become disenchanted
Seeing such a miserable corpse.
In me, sensual desire arose —
Blind, I was bound.

Faster than boiling rice,
I left that place.
Mindful, clearly comprehending,
I came, sat to one side.

Then I attended to it,
Reflecting wisely —
The danger became clear,
I dwelt in disenchantment.

And my mind was liberated.
Seeing the Dhamma as it is,
I attained the three true knowledges,
Accomplishing the Buddha’s teaching.

title: “Monks, a jackal saw a tortoise from afar and approached it. Having approached, it stood to one side and thought: ‘When this tortoise stretches out…
content: “Monks, a jackal saw a tortoise from afar and approached it. Having approached, it stood to one side and thought: ‘When this tortoise stretches out any of its limbs or its neck, I will seize it right there, break it, and eat it.’ But, monks, because the tortoise did not stretch out any limb or its neck, the jackal became disenchanted with the tortoise and left, not having gained an opportunity. So too, monks, Māra constantly and relentlessly stands in ambush for you, thinking: ‘Perhaps I can gain an opportunity through the eye … through the tongue … through the mind.’ Therefore, monks, guard the sense faculties. When you see a form with the eye, do not grasp the general feature, do not grasp the particular feature. Those causes whereby, if the eye faculty were not restrained, covetousness, sorrow, evil, unwholesome states would arise — restrain that cause, guard the eye, practice restraint of the eye. When you hear a sound … smell an odor … taste a flavor … feel a touch … cognize a phenomenon with the mind, do not grasp the general feature, do not grasp the particular feature. Those causes whereby, if the mind faculty were not restrained, covetousness, sorrow, evil, unwholesome states would arise — restrain that cause, guard the mind, practice restraint of the mind. Monks, when you live guarding the sense faculties, Māra will become disenchanted with you and leave, not gaining an opportunity, just like the jackal with the tortoise.”
